boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Buffington Island record (July 19, 1863) in Morgan's Raid in Kentucky, Indiana, and Ohio [July 1863]. The July 20 surrender near the Hocking and the pursuit to Salineville are outside this interval. The raid's start strength, detachments, captures and campaign effects span July 2–26 and several engagements; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen field reads 'Brigades: 4,700 total (US 3,000; CS 1,700)' and the live field agrees. Duke says his side was scarcely 1,900 strong, gives Hobson 3,000 and Judah several thousand, and says Judah's command was reported to be eight or ten thousand strong; his two engaged regiments were each not more than 250 strong. Hobson says the combined commands numbered about 2,500 when he took command at Lebanon on July 6, and that only a small portion of his command was present when Judah arrived.
claims.rationale: Duke's 1,900 differs from the frozen 1,700; Hobson's July 6 figure predates the engagement. None is adopted as matched opening strength.

claims.value: Duke says an earthwork with two heavy guns commanded the ford, the valley was about a mile long and perhaps 800 yards wide at its southern end with a ridge on its western side, and the river had risen several feet in the previous week. Kautz's dispatch, quoted by Hobson, says the river was too high to ford; Hobson says citizens told him the hills were impassable.
claims.rationale: Positions and water level from interested accounts; the work was abandoned before dawn. No map or gauge verification.

claims.rationale: Stated aims from interested accounts; Duke's are his reading of Morgan's intent.

claims.value: NPS puts the pursuing columns under Hobson's overall direction and says Kautz's and Judah's brigades attacked. Hobson says Judah assumed command of the whole force over his protest, leaving him detained with his staff. Duke says an order to rally to horses was issued by some one he does not name, and that he and Colonel Johnson decided together to withdraw. The frozen commanders are Hobson and Morgan, both Brigadier Generals.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a summary and interested accounts; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says Morgan and about 400 men escaped encirclement during the night by a narrow woods path and the rest surrendered. Duke says between 1,100 and 1,200 men retreated with Morgan and some 300 of them crossed the river about twenty miles above. Hobson calls the rout complete and says Duke and his command surrendered to a sergeant of the Ninth Michigan Cavalry.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The escape counts differ in scope and timing.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields give 925 (US 25; CS 900). Duke says about 700 prisoners were taken and some twenty-odd of his men killed by musketry, the Union losing quite as many. Hobson says his command's casualties did not exceed 5 or 6, gives 57 Confederate killed on a militia surgeon's report, and says he could not give the exact number of prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Judah's, Kautz's and Sanders's reports, the gunboat reports and the Confederate prisoner rolls remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Duke's History of Morgan's Cavalry (1867) is an interested Confederate participant history: Duke commanded a brigade on the raid by his own account and was captured at Buffington, so his account of later days is not eyewitness. The Burnside, Hobson and Shackelford reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIII, Part 1, are interested Union accounts. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
